jobs.excerpt: Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO)About the RoleWe are seeking an accomplished and strategically minded Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO) to lead the financial strategy, performance, capital management, investment finance, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investments Group.
jobs.description:
Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and strategically minded Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO) to lead the financial strategy, performance, capital management, investment finance, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investments Group.

The Group CFO will have enterprise-wide responsibility for the Group's financial affairs, overseeing finance across subsidiaries, business units, investment entities, and operating companies.

As a key member of the Group Executive Leadership Team, the Group CFO will serve as a strategic advisor to the Group CEO, President, Board, Investment Committee, and other senior stakeholders, ensuring disciplined capital allocation, strong financial performance, balance-sheet resilience, regulatory compliance, and long-term shareholder value creation.

The role requires a sophisticated financial leader with experience across insurance, investment management, asset management, financial services, corporate finance, capital markets, and regulated financial institutions.

Key Responsibilities

1. Group Financial Strategy & Leadership

Develop and execute the Group's overall financial strategy in alignment with corporate objectives.

Provide strategic financial advice to the Group CEO, President, Board, and Executive Committee.

Establish Group-wide financial policies, standards, controls, and performance frameworks.

Ensure effective financial governance across subsidiaries, business units, joint ventures, and investment entities.

Lead the development of the Group's long-term financial and capital strategy.

2. Group P&L & Financial Performance

Assume overall responsibility for the Group's financial performance, profitability, balance sheet, cash flow, and capital position.

Monitor performance across all subsidiaries and business lines.

Drive sustainable earnings growth, expense efficiency, and return on capital.

Establish Group-wide financial KPIs and performance dashboards.

Challenge business-unit leadership on financial performance and corrective actions.

3. Financial Planning & Performance Management

Lead Group-wide annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning.

Develop financial scenarios and stress tests to support strategic decision-making.

Consolidate financial plans across subsidiaries and investment businesses.

Monitor actual performance against budgets, forecasts, and strategic objectives.

Strengthen management reporting and financial analytics.

4. Insurance Finance

Provide executive oversight of financial management across insurance businesses.

Monitor premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, underwriting results, and insurance profitability.

Oversee financial analysis of loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting margins.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk functions to understand financial exposures.

Provide financial input into product profitability, pricing, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions.

5. Investment & Asset Management Finance

Provide Group-level financial oversight of investment portfolios and investment businesses.

Partner with the Chief Investment Officer (CIO) and Investment Committee on investment strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, portfolio returns, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted performance.

Evaluate strategic investment opportunities and major portfolio decisions.

Ensure investment activities support the Group's liabilities, capital objectives, liquidity needs, and risk appetite.

6. Group Capital & Solvency Management

Lead Group-wide capital planning and capital optimization.

Monitor capital adequacy, solvency, leverage, liquidity, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize capital deployment across subsidiaries and business lines.

Assess the capital implications of acquisitions, investments, dividends, growth initiatives, and strategic transactions.

Partner with Risk and Actuarial leadership on capital and solvency assessments.

7. Asset-Liability Management

Provide executive oversight of asset-liability management (ALM) across relevant insurance and investment businesses.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support balance-sheet optimization and financial stress-testing initiatives.

8. Treasury & Liquidity

Lead Group treasury, liquidity, cash management, and banking relationships.

Establish Group-wide liquidity policies and funding strategies.

Optimize cash across subsidiaries while maintaining appropriate regulatory and operational liquidity.

Oversee debt facilities, guarantees, intercompany funding, and treasury risk.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

9. Capital Raising & Financing

Lead Group-level financing and capital-raising initiatives.

Develop relationships with banks, institutional investors, private equity firms, development-finance institutions, debt providers, and capital-market participants.

Oversee debt issuance, refinancing, capital injections, and other funding strategies.

Optimize the Group's capital structure and cost of capital.

Ensure funding capacity supports strategic growth.

10. M&A, Investments & Corporate Development

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, disposals, strategic investments, and joint ventures.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and deal structuring.

Assess the impact of transactions on earnings, capital, solvency, liquidity, and shareholder value.

Partner with the CEO and Board on major strategic transactions.

Oversee financial integration and post-transaction performance.

11. Group Financial Reporting & Consolidation

Ensure accurate and timely consolidated financial reporting across the Group.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and Board reporting.

Establish consistent accounting and reporting standards across subsidiaries.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Maintain strong relationships with external auditors and professional advisers.

12. Regulatory & Governance

Maintain strong financial governance across the Group.

Ensure compliance with applicable insurance, investment, corporate, tax, and financial regulations.

Manage relationships with regulators, auditors, rating agencies, and other external stakeholders.

Establish effective internal controls and financial policies.

Ensure appropriate governance across subsidiaries, SPVs, joint ventures, and investment entities.

13. Financial Risk Management

Establish and oversee the Group's financial risk-management framework.

Monitor market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, investment, interest-rate, FX, and operational financial risks.

Establish appropriate stress-testing and contingency-planning processes.

Work closely with the Group CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and business leaders to manage enterprise-wide risk.

14. Tax Strategy

Oversee Group-wide tax planning, compliance, reporting, and risk management.

Ensure appropriate tax governance across subsidiaries and jurisdictions.

Identify opportunities for legitimate tax efficiency.

Monitor changes in tax and regulatory requirements affecting the Group.

15. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, lenders, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Lead financial communications to the Board and key investors.

Support investor presentations, annual reports, strategic reviews, and capital-market activities.

Clearly communicate the Group's financial strategy, performance, and outlook.

16. Finance Transformation

Modernize the Group's finance operating model, systems, processes, and reporting infrastructure.

Strengthen ERP, FP&A, consolidation, business intelligence, and financial analytics capabilities.

Drive automation and digital transformation across finance.

Improve transparency and real-time visibility across subsidiaries and business units.

17. Leadership & Organizational Development

Lead the Group Finance function and senior finance leadership across subsidiaries.

Develop a high-performing, commercially focused finance organization.

Establish common standards, talent-development programs, and succession plans.

Build strong relationships with subsidiary CFOs and Finance Directors.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and value creation.

Key Performance Indicators

The Group CFO will be accountable for:

Group revenue and earnings growth

Group EBITDA / net income performance

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Insurance underwriting profitability

Combined ratio / loss ratio performance

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow strength

Balance-sheet optimization

Cost of capital

Capital-raising effectiveness

M&A and strategic-investment performance

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and reporting compliance

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

18+ years of progressive finance experience, including substantial Group or enterprise-level leadership.

Previous experience as Group CFO, CFO, Deputy Group CFO, Group Finance Director, Finance Director, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, investment management, asset management, banking, pensions, reinsurance, or diversified financial services.

Proven experience managing complex group structures, subsidiaries, investment entities, and regulated businesses.

Strong understanding of insurance financial reporting, capital and solvency requirements, investment portfolios, and balance-sheet management.

Demonstrated experience in capital allocation, treasury, liquidity, financial planning, and enterprise risk.

Experience working directly with Boards, CEOs, regulators, auditors, investors, lenders, and rating agencies.

Preferred Experience

Previous Group CFO experience within a diversified insurance or investment group.

Experience covering both insurance operations and investment/asset-management businesses.

Exposure to life insurance, general insurance, reinsurance, pensions, or institutional investment.

Experience managing significant investment portfolios and ALM.

Proven experience with M&A, capital raising, restructuring, strategic investments, or international expansion.

Experience across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments.

Experience working with international institutional investors or rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is advantageous.

Additional insurance, investment, actuarial, or risk-management qualifications are desirable.

Core Competencies

Group Financial Leadership

Corporate Finance

Insurance Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Capital Allocation

M&A & Corporate Development

Regulatory Reporting

Risk Management

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Finance Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful Group CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially astute, and financially rigorous

Comfortable operating across complex group structures

Strong in capital allocation and investment decisions

Experienced in highly regulated environments

A sophisticated communicator at Board and investor level

Strong in balance-sheet and liquidity management

Comfortable challenging business leaders and driving accountability

Able to balance growth, profitability, capital, liquidity, and risk

An effective partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, Chief Actuary, and subsidiary CEOs

A transformational leader capable of building a world-class Group Finance function

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

jobs.description:
Company: Coherence OS
Location: Remote (Global)
Compensation: Equity-Only (Slicing Pie) → Cash at Break-Even

We’re building Coherence OS because we believe the next era of technology requires more than speed and scale — it requires meaning, integrity, and systems that hold over time.

This role isn’t for someone looking for a job. It’s for someone who wants to build infrastructure they can stand behind years from now, alongside a small, serious team that values fairness, clarity, and real ownership.

We use the Slicing Pie model because it’s the only compensation system we’ve found that actually treats people like adults: contribution in equals ownership earned, dollar for dollar. If that resonates with you — not as a gamble, but as a principle — you’ll probably feel at home here.

About Coherence OS

Coherence OS is an AI-native operating system focused on preserving human meaning, identity, and ethical coherence in the age of advanced automation.

We are building foundational infrastructure intended to support long-lived, global-scale systems — not short-term SaaS experiments.

This role is for someone who wants to build the substrate, not just ship tickets.

Company Stage & Visibility

Coherence OS is in its earliest build phase. We are intentionally operating with a minimal public footprint while core systems, filings, and internal foundations are being finalized.

We do not have a public website yet. Full context about the company, mission, and roadmap will be shared during the interview process.

This role is part of the initial engineering team and is best suited for candidates who are comfortable joining early, helping shape foundational systems, and building before everything is public.

Position

We are seeking a skilled Infrastructure Engineer to design, build, and maintain the infrastructure that powers our applications and services. In this role, you will work closely with engineering, data, and security teams to ensure our systems are scalable, reliable, secure, and highly available.

The ideal candidate has strong experience with cloud platforms, infrastructure automation, and modern DevOps practices, and is passionate about improving system performance and developer productivity.

Responsibilities

Infrastructure Design & Development

  • Design, implement, and maintain scalable cloud infrastructure.
  • Build highly available and fault-tolerant systems.
  • Architect solutions across compute, storage, networking, and security layers.

Infrastructure as Code (IaC)

  • Develop and maintain infrastructure using Terraform.
  • Automate provisioning and configuration of infrastructure environments.
  • Maintain version-controlled infrastructure repositories.

Cloud Platform Management

  • Manage cloud environment - GCP.
  • Optimize infrastructure costs and performance.
  • Implement high-availability and disaster recovery strategies.

CI/CD & Deployment Automation

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for automated deployments.
  • Support containerized application deployments using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Improve deployment reliability and release processes.

Security & Compliance

  • Implement secure infrastructure practices including IAM, network policies, and access controls.
  • Work with security teams to enforce best practices and compliance standards.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Kubernetes or container-based platforms.
  • Experience with monitoring tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, or Datadog.
  • Experience with serverless or cloud-native architectures.

jobs.excerpt: Head of Marketing, B2B GrowthIf you are a hands-on B2B marketing builder who wants real ownership—not a large inherited team—this is an opportunity to build the marketing engine for an established, growing B2B organization with complementary professional-services and software offerings.
jobs.description:
Head of Marketing, B2B Growth

If you are a hands-on B2B marketing builder who wants real ownership—not a large inherited team—this is an opportunity to build the marketing engine for an established, growing B2B organization with complementary professional-services and software offerings. You will have meaningful autonomy, a broad mandate, and compensation of $165,000–$200,000 to personally shape the strategy, messaging, campaigns, enablement, measurement, and AI-enabled workflows that help the business scale.

The Opportunity

Our client is an established B2B organization with both relationship-led professional-services revenue and recurring software revenue. The company has grown through strong market relationships and selective marketing support, and now needs one accountable marketing owner to create a more repeatable, measurable, modern growth function.

This is initially a true department-of-one role. You may use contractors or vendors where they create leverage, but this is not a strategy-only executive seat and not a people-management-first role. The right person wants to build the plan, write the copy, shape positioning, launch campaigns, improve systems, and create momentum before every condition is perfect.

The Mandate

You will own marketing across two related but different B2B commercial motions: a relationship-led services business and a software business with recurring revenue dynamics. Success requires commercial judgment, fast learning, strong execution, and the ability to produce credible work quickly in a complex B2B environment.

What You Will Own

  • Build and run a focused marketing plan tied to company goals, revenue priorities, sales needs, campaign opportunities, and measurable progress.
  • Clarify ICPs, buyer problems, positioning, offers, messaging, and channel priorities across professional-services and software motions.
  • Personally create and improve campaigns, landing pages, email, LinkedIn content, thought leadership, case studies, event follow-up, and sales materials.
  • Translate complex B2B topics into clear, credible, buyer-relevant messaging without relying on generic agency output or low-quality AI content.
  • Build a consistent content, campaign, and demand-generation engine that improves shipping velocity, market visibility, and sales usefulness.
  • Partner with senior leaders, sales, product, and subject-matter experts to turn business insight into practical marketing work without becoming a reactive ticket-taker.
  • Improve marketing operations, funnel visibility, reporting, testing, and decision-making from imperfect historical data.
  • Use vendors selectively, rationalize spend, and increase output per dollar while staying personally close enough to the work to raise quality.

What Success Looks Like

In the first year, you will establish a clear marketing plan and operating cadence, create a usable messaging foundation, launch a steady content and campaign rhythm, improve measurement, and build repeatable sales-enablement and event-follow-up motions. The business should see clearer priorities, better marketing throughput, stronger stakeholder trust, and measurable progress in qualified demand, engagement, pipeline influence, or another agreed commercial indicator.

Required Qualifications

  • Substantive B2B marketing experience. This is not a consumer-marketing role.
  • Recent, genuine department-of-one or extremely lean-team ownership where you personally produced and shipped work.
  • Broad experience across demand generation, positioning, content, campaigns, sales enablement, marketing operations, and measurement.
  • Ability to set strategy and execute: you can write, launch, analyze, iterate, and improve the work yourself.
  • Strong copy judgment and the writing ability to make complex B2B topics clear, specific, and commercially useful.
  • Enough visual taste to prevent generic, off-brand, or visibly low-quality output, whether you create assets yourself or direct others.
  • Demonstrable AI-native execution through real workflows, agents, automations, prototypes, campaigns, analysis, or shipped work products—not just familiarity with tools.
  • Comfort creating practical measurement and making decisions despite messy data or incomplete historical reporting.
  • Fast learning, entrepreneurial ownership, prioritization, follow-through, and low-ego partnership with senior stakeholders.
  • Commercial understanding that relationship-led professional-services revenue and recurring software revenue require different marketing motions.
  • Remote United States availability with strong alignment to East Coast working hours.

Preferred Background

Experience marketing both B2B professional services and B2B software is strongly preferred because this role spans two different commercial motions. That said, experience in both is not an automatic knockout if you bring exceptional B2B experience, strong commercial judgment, fast learning, and credible transferable evidence.

Helpful backgrounds may include hands-on Head of Marketing, Director of Marketing, Senior Marketing Manager, Demand Generation, Growth Marketing, or broad B2B marketing ownership in a resource-constrained startup, growth company, professional-services firm, software company, regulated industry, or other complex B2B environment.

AI-Enabled Work Demonstration

Finalists should expect to demonstrate a real AI-enabled marketing workflow they have built or used in practice. The goal is to understand how you research, draft, automate, analyze, validate, and apply judgment—not to reward tool lists or generic prompting language.

Work Model, Travel, and Compensation

  • Remote role for U.S.-based candidates.
  • Strong alignment with East Coast working hours is required.
  • Occasional travel for company meetings, industry events, or conferences may be required.
  • Compensation range: $165,000–$200,000 annually.

Compensation

  • Deliver Family-Centered Psychotherapy: Provide evidence-based individual, joint family, and parent/guardian teletherapy for youth (ages 12–26) at high or critical risk of suicide, utilizing family-systems frameworks, C-CBT, DBT skills, and Motivational Interviewing.

  • Maintain Fee-for-Service & Medicaid Compliance: Complete high-integrity, timely clinical documentation (DAP) that explicitly substantiates medical necessity, suicide risk levels, family interventions, and whole-person care for Medicaid Fee-for-Service (FFS) billing.

  • Integrate Care Infrastructure & Panel Tracking: Actively participate in interdisciplinary huddles, maintain registry accuracy, and monitor personal KPIs (billable hours, documentation turnaround, and show rates) to optimize clinical outcomes across the program panel.

  • Problem Solving: Identifies needs and takes independent action to implement change when and where it is needed; results oriented. Ability to plan, organize, manage time, and prioritize multiple tasks and assignments.
  • Ability to provide case management in routine and crisis situations.
  • Self-motivated, team player, adaptable with a strong sense of urgency in a fast-paced

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in psychology, social work, or other applicable behavioral health discipline from an accredited college or university is required.
  • Licensure: Current Washington Department of Health (WA DOH) independent behavioral health license. Eligible licenses include:
    • Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW)

  • Two or more years of direct experience working with adolescents and adults in the behavioral health field required. Experience in suicide prevention strongly preferred.
  • Crisis intervention training and experience required.
  • Knowledge of local resources, social determinants of health, mental health, substance use disorders, interpersonal violence, and social issues.

jobs.excerpt: Staff Product Designer, Guest & DiscoveryCompanyCollaborative Boating operates Boatsetter and GetMyBoat, the two largest marketplaces for getting on the water, now converging into one platform.
jobs.description:
Staff Product Designer, Guest & Discovery

Company

Collaborative Boating operates Boatsetter and GetMyBoat, the two largest marketplaces for getting on the water, now converging into one platform. Guests arrive wanting something specific — a fishing trip, a sunset cruise, a birthday on a pontoon — and we connect them to the captains, operators, and owners who can make it happen. Finding and booking a day outside should be as easy and intuitive as booking a flight.

The problem

Search is changing under us. Guests arrive with intent expressed in natural language, increasingly through an AI assistant instead of a search box, and increasingly on a surface we don't own. Answering that with a chatbot is the obvious move and the wrong one: choosing between boats is a parallel, visual, comparison task, and a conversation is sequential. The work is holding both — a visual discovery experience built for comparison, and a compact, structured expression of a listing that holds up when a third-party assistant renders it in a layout we didn't design.

The center of gravity is the search results card. It's the smallest unit of persuasion we have: a handful of facts, ordered, that a guest uses to decide whether to look closer. Which facts earn a place, in what order, and how that adapts from "boat rental Miami" to "something fun for eight people Saturday" — that's the problem. It's an information design problem before it's a visual one.

What you'll own

  • The end-to-end guest discovery experience — search, filtering and refinement, results, map and list, the listing page, and the paths in from organic search and AI assistants. Coherence across both brands and web plus mobile is yours.
  • The information hierarchy of the results card, defended with evidence, across guest intents and every state the data actually produces: missing photos, no reviews yet, a price range instead of a price, partial availability.
  • Interfaces over a system that infers. Make what it inferred legible, make correcting it easy, and reduce verification labor rather than creating it — a guest who has to double-check our answer has been handed our work.
  • Surfaces we don't render. With engineering, shape the structured expression of an experience, an offer, and an operator so it survives being summarized, quoted, or laid out by someone else's assistant.
  • Continuous discovery with your pod — a Product Manager and an engineering tech lead. Choose the cheapest artifact that answers the open question; spend fidelity when a decision is actually being committed.

How we work

Five things worth knowing before you apply. They aren't universal, and here they aren't negotiable.

Problem, then system, then experience

We frame the problem, then settle the shape of the system — entities, states, edge cases — and only then design the experience within it. Your rough exploration runs alongside the system design and improves it; committed fidelity comes later. In practice that means days of useful work before there's a screen worth showing, and arguing about data models with your tech lead while the design is still loose. If you need a settled brief before you can start, this will be frustrating.

Discovery is ongoing, not a handed off spec

You talk to guests and operators directly. You bring opportunities forward rather than receiving them. There's no research team handing you findings and no Product Manager writing you requirements — the pod owns the outcome and you're one third of it. We believe the commercial results follow from understanding these customers better than anyone else does, which is why the understanding isn't delegated to a function.

We ask what moved, not what shipped

You define the signal before release and watch it after. Hitting the number you set is the floor, not the finish — the work worth remembering beat it, and we'd rather you aim at that and miss than aim at the floor and land. Sometimes the answer is that your design didn't work, you say so plainly, and we kill it. If measurement feels like a threat to the craft rather than part of it, this will be a hard place to work.

We ship in days, not quarters

Work goes live the day it's ready — no launch calendar, no approval chain. The pod decides and it goes out. Fast here means small and finished, not big and rough: a narrow slice with its states designed and its accessibility handled, in front of real guests this week, then the next slice. The quality bar doesn't move; the amount of surface you hold before releasing does. What you give up is the reveal — your work is live while it's still incomplete in aggregate, and you correct in the open rather than perfecting behind a curtain. Designers who need to control the whole surface before anyone sees it will find this hard.

We cross lines, and we bet on each other

Titles and team boundaries carry little weight here. You'll be inside the domain model with an engineer, in a support queue reading what operators actually complain about, in a pricing conversation that isn't nominally yours. Ask for help early and give it generously. The standing assumption is that the person next to you is good and worth backing before they've proven it to you — and we expect the same read on you.

We work inside the design system by default; a new pattern has to earn itself against what already exists. WCAG 2.1 AA is an accepted platform standard, not a per-feature negotiation.

What you need to have done

  • Held substantial ownership of search, browse, or discovery in a two-sided marketplace — relevance surfaces, faceted filtering, availability and pricing display, map plus list, comparison.
  • Designed information you can defend. Walk us through a dense comparison surface you built: why each element is there, why it's ordered that way, what you removed, and what removing it cost.
  • Designed over a system that infers, ranks, or predicts — communicating state and confidence in real time, and designing the correction path for when the system is wrong.
  • Formed a point of view on search in an AI-driven world, including where conversation doesn't belong. We'd rather you disagree with us than agree quickly.

What also helps

Fluency with entities, states, and contracts alongside your tech lead. Restraint and typographic craft in high-information surfaces. AI tools in your own practice. Search relevance literacy, structured data and schema work, third-party assistant surfaces, or travel, hospitality, and local-services search at scale are each a plus rather than a requirement.

Your portfolio

Send work, not a slide deck about process. Two or three cases at depth. For at least one: the problem and how you knew it was real, what you tried and abandoned, the hierarchy decisions and their rationale, the states you designed for, what shipped, and what it changed. Include something that didn't work. Roughness is fine — we care about the reasoning.

Practicals

Remote, with high overlap in United States Eastern hours. You'll join a five-person design team, report to our Director of Design, and be the dedicated designer in this pod. Relevant degrees in design, HCI, or information architecture are welcome and not required — portfolio and shipped, measured work outweigh credentials.

We are building the next generation of healthcare technology — an AI-native product organization that moves fast, operates with intention, and ships products that meaningfully improve care. The Head of Transformation is a senior operating role that sits at the center of that mission in product.

Reporting directly to the Chief Product Officer, you will serve as a force-multiplier for the CPO — translating vision into operating rhythm, building the connective tissue across product, design, engineering, and the business, and ensuring that the organization's most important bets get the attention, structure, and follow-through they deserve.

The right candidate is equally comfortable writing a strategy memo, facilitating a cross-functional alignment session, designing a planning process from scratch, and rolling up their sleeves to program management a strategic project.

A Day in the Life

CPO Leverage & Office of the CPO

  • Serve as the CPO's thought partner and operational deputy, preparing briefing materials, driving follow-through on key initiatives, and acting as a proxy in select forums.
  • Own the CPO's planning calendar: quarterly business reviews, product leadership offsites, board and executive updates, and annual planning cycles.
  • Distil complex, cross-functional inputs into crisp written recommendations, decision documents, and narratives for senior audiences.

Product Operations & Operating Rhythm

  • Design and stand up the product operating model for an AI-native organization — including portfolio prioritization, OKR processes, roadmap governance, and cross-functional rituals.
  • Build lightweight, high-signal reporting cadences that give the CPO and product leadership real-time visibility into progress, risks, and decisions.
  • Drive quarterly and annual planning: coordinating inputs from product, engineering, design, data science, and go-to-market teams into a coherent, executable plan.
  • Identify operational inefficiencies and eliminate them — the goal is a product organization that ships faster and with less friction, not more process.

Transformation & Strategic Initiatives

  • Lead high-priority transformation programs on behalf of the CPO — spanning organizational design, AI adoption, new capability builds, and cross-functional change management.
  • Act as a program manager for initiatives that cut across multiple teams and do not have a natural single owner.
  • Build the infrastructure for how the product organization makes and communicates decisions — from DACI frameworks to async-first working norms.
  • Partner with People, Finance, and Legal as needed to bring structure to people and resource decisions in the product org.

AI-Native Ways of Working

  • Help shape what it means to operate as an AI-native product organization — piloting new tools, workflows, and norms and socializing them across the team.
  • Build muscle around how the product organization consumes, generates, and acts on AI-driven insights.
  • Partner with product and design leadership to embed AI-first thinking into how we scope, prototype, and evaluate work.

What You Need

  • 7–12+ years of experience in product management, strategy, management consulting, chief of staff, or business operations roles — ideally with meaningful time in a high-growth technology or healthcare technology company.
  • Track record of building from scratch. You have stood up new processes, teams, or functions and know how to earn buy-in without authority.
  • Familiarity with AI tooling and modern product operating models. You are curious and opinionated about how AI changes how teams work, and you have practical experience putting AI to use.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can write a crisp one-pager for the CEO and a detailed PRD spec in the same week. You tailor your message to the audience.
  • Strong product intuition. You do not need to be a product manager, but you need to speak the language fluently — roadmaps, trade-offs, customer insight, technical constraints.
  • Structured thinking under ambiguity. You can hold complexity, work through incomplete information, and still drive decisions forward.
  • Genuine comfort as an individual contributor. You are not waiting to manage people. You are energised by the idea of building something from the ground up and rolling up your sleeves.
  • High emotional intelligence and organisational savvy. You build trust quickly, navigate competing priorities with empathy, and know how to influence without creating friction.

We offer competitive benefits to set you up for success in and outside of work.

Here’s What We Offer

  • Generous Paid Time Off: Recharge and relax with 20 days of fixed time off per year, in addition to company holidays—because we believe work-life balance fuels performance.
  • Best-in-Class Parental Leave: Spend quality time with your growing family. We offer one of the industry’s most generous parental leave policies to support you during life’s most important moments.
  • Recognition & Rewards: We celebrate wins—big and small. Get rewarded with monetary incentives and company-wide recognition for your impact and dedication. Your hard work won’t go unnoticed.

The Bet We're Making

We bet on speed of thinking and quality of work with an agent, not years of stack. We want an engineer who, with an AI agent, ships like a stronger engineer — because they lead the agent instead of clicking "accept."

You write a plan, break work into steps, verify each step, reason about the output, and give precise next instructions. You don't trust code you haven't verified. If your style is "generate it and click around the UI until it seems to work," this isn't for you — and vice versa.

You Care Why, Not Just How

You engage with the business problem, not just the ticket. You don't need to know travel — the domain is specific and nobody arrives knowing it. What matters is that you get curious about why a feature exists, who needs it, and what changes once it ships. When a business stakeholder comes to you, that conversation is interesting, not an interruption. That habit is a large part of what we're selecting for.

Tech Stack

  • Backend: Python (SQLAlchemy, GraphQL, PostgreSQL) — complex queries against a rich data model. Writing complex SQL itself is something an agent helps with. The judgment around it is on you.

At Fuelerate, we move fast and care about results.We value ownership, speed, accountability, and high standards.That means owning your numbers. Following up when others stop. Learning from lost deals. Getting better every week. And never waiting for someone else to push an opportunity forward.You’ll have support, training, and a calendar of opportunities. This is not primarily a prospecting role.We’re building the acquisition engine to keep our closers busy. You may help with other sales activities while ramping, but your main responsibility is closing.

Qualified Call VolumeOur bottleneck is sales capacity, not acquisition. Once ramped, our goal is to give you 6–8 qualified calls per day.

📋 Taken en verantwoordelijkheden

Presentatie

Dit programma is ingebed in de directie Politie Informatie en ICT, die instaat voor de voorbereiding van beleid en regels rond informatiebeheer en -verwerking, de ontwikkeling van het politie-informatieconcept, het bepalen van technische normen en standaarden en de implementatie van informatie- en communicatiesystemen.

Project

Automatische kentekenplaatherkenning (Automatic Number Plate Recognition, ANPR) maakt gebruik van intelligente camera’s die nummerplaten herkennen. De gescande nummerplaten worden vervolgens vergeleken met beschikbare gegevens, bijvoorbeeld over gestolen of geseinde voertuigen of voertuigen die al dan niet in bepaalde zones mogen rijden. Binnen deze context wordt ANPR ingezet voor verkeersveiligheid en gerechtelijke opdrachten.

Missie

Als business analist binnen het ANPR-domein ondersteun je analyses binnen het domein verkeer en vertaal je behoeften vanop het terrein naar concrete voorstellen voor de stabilisatie en modernisering van het ANPR-systeem. Daarbij werk je aan uiteenlopende initiatieven, zoals functionele uitbreidingen, software-upgrades, procesmodellering (as-is/to-be) en het heroriënteren van bestaande oplossingen en materiaal.

Je brengt initiatieven samen in een gestructureerde aanpak, met aandacht voor haalbaarheid, prioriteiten, timing, budget en afhankelijkheden. Je werkt nauw samen met interne stakeholders, waaronder kerngebruikers, IT-architecten, projectmanagers, gegevensexperten, analisten en software engineers, en stemt waar nodig af met externe partners. Dankzij je technisch inzicht neem je een adviserende en faciliterende rol op naar zowel management als operationele diensten. Je bouwt snel domeinkennis op en documenteert die zorgvuldig om kennisborging en overdracht te verzekeren.

Je kan vlot schakelen tussen verschillende onderwerpen en past je aan wisselende prioriteiten aan.

Taken en verantwoordelijkheden:

  • Hoofdtaken:
    • Zorgen dat requirements en standaarden voor alle verkeersinitiatieven binnen het ANPR-programma duidelijk en volledig zijn uitgewerkt.
    • Processen in kaart brengen en analyseren, inclusief as-is- en to-be-modellen.
    • Taken, afhankelijkheden en risico’s identificeren en opvolgen.
    • De voortgang rapporteren aan stakeholders, met aandacht voor status, problemen, bottlenecks, risico’s, mitigerende maatregelen en beslissingen in een decision log.
    • Kwaliteitsbeheerplannen opzetten en onderhouden zodat resultaten voldoen aan de vereiste normen.
    • Stakeholdermanagement opnemen en duurzame relaties uitbouwen met interne belanghebbenden, eindgebruikers en externe partners.
    • Informatie en analyses op een gestructureerde manier documenteren voor rapportering, kennisborging en overdracht.
  • Neventaken:
    • Bijdragen aan een toekomstvisie voor een stabiel ANPR-ecosysteem op lange termijn, rekening houdend met capaciteitsgroei, nieuwe technologieën en integraties met andere systemen.
    • Nieuwe ontwikkelingen in ANPR-technologie en relevante wet- en regelgeving opvolgen en deze inzichten verwerken in analyses en adviezen.
    • Input aanleveren voor DPIA’s, risico-analyses en gelijkaardige trajecten in samenwerking met gegevensbeschermingsexperten.

📝 Jouw profiel

  • Minstens vijf jaar hands-on ervaring in business analyse en/of het begeleiden van ICT-projecten.
  • Aantoonbare ervaring in complexe IT-omgevingen binnen overheidsinstanties of de publieke sector.
  • Ervaring met analysemethodologieën en tools, zoals bedrijfsprocesmodellering, requirements management en systemen voor projectopvolging.
  • Bekendheid met MS Visio, Power BI, Jira, Confluence of vergelijkbare tools is een plus.
  • Sterk analytisch vermogen en probleemoplossende vaardigheden, met oog voor detail én voor het bredere geheel.
  • Je kan grote hoeveelheden informatie structureren, neutraal samenvatten en onderbouwde conclusies formuleren.
  • Frans of Nederlands als moedertaal, met een sterke passieve kennis van de andere landstaal om in een tweetalige context te functioneren. Een goede kennis van het Engels is een troef voor technische documentatie.
  • Affiniteit met of ervaring in ANPR-systemen, cameratechnologie en/of de vaststellingsketen binnen verkeer is een meerwaarde.
  • Je werkt proactief, resultaatgericht en gestructureerd, neemt initiatief en kan zelfstandig prioriteiten beheren.
  • Je communiceert helder, zowel schriftelijk als mondeling, en kan verschillende stakeholders inhoudelijk op één lijn brengen.
  • Discretie en betrouwbaarheid zijn essentieel gezien de gevoelige aard van de informatie.

⚠️ This position is offered as a full-time role.

💼 Aanbod

Je zal deel uitmaken van een groeiende KMO met ruimte voor initiatief en persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Wij zorgen ervoor dat je in een uitdagende maar aangename werkomgeving terecht komt met leuke collega's. We’re looking for an organized, creative, and proactive Part-Time Social Media Manager to support the day-to-day management and ongoing development of social media across multiple brands and projects.

This role will initially focus on managing social calendars, coordinating content, scheduling and publishing posts, and ensuring everything goes live accurately and on time. As you become familiar with our brands and audiences, we’d also like you to take greater ownership of content ideation, caption writing, and content creation.

What You’ll Do

  • Manage and maintain social media content calendars across multiple accounts

  • Schedule and publish content across platforms including LinkedIn, Instagram, X/Twitter, Facebook, and other relevant channels

  • Review content before publishing to ensure copy, creative, links, tags, and formatting are correct

  • Write and refine social media captions in line with each brand’s voice

  • Develop and propose new social media content ideas

  • Create social-first content for select brands, including simple graphics, posts, stories, and other platform-appropriate content

  • Help build out content calendars by identifying relevant topics, trends, campaigns, and opportunities

  • Coordinate with designers, copywriters, and internal team members when additional creative support is required

  • Track upcoming posts, campaigns, events, launches, and key dates

  • Monitor scheduled content and confirm posts have published correctly

  • Maintain consistency in brand voice, messaging, and visual presentation

  • Monitor comments, messages, mentions, and basic audience engagement

  • Flag questions, issues, or opportunities that require input from the wider team

  • Support social content for events, announcements, campaigns, and other marketing initiatives

  • Keep social media assets and content organized

  • Provide basic reporting on content performance and engagement

  • Use performance insights to recommend improvements to content, posting cadence, and overall social presence

What We’re Looking For

  • Previous experience managing social media for brands or businesses

  • Strong writing and caption-creation skills

  • A good eye for engaging, platform-appropriate social content

  • Ability to generate content ideas rather than relying solely on content provided by others

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail

  • Experience with social media scheduling and management tools

  • Comfortable managing multiple brands, accounts, and deadlines simultaneously

  • Ability to understand and adapt to different brand voices and audiences

  • Able to work independently and proactively follow up on missing content or approvals

  • Reliable and comfortable working within a remote, fast-moving team

  • Availability that overlaps with CET business hours

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with an agency or managing multiple client accounts

  • Canva or other basic design/content creation skills

  • Experience creating short-form social content

  • Experience with project management tools such as Jira, Basecamp, Monday.com, or similar

  • Familiarity with social analytics and reporting

  • Experience supporting event or conference-related social content

About the Role

This is a hands-on role combining social media management, coordination, and content creation. Initially, the priority will be ensuring our social operation runs smoothly — content is organized, reviewed, scheduled, published, and monitored consistently.

We’re looking for someone who can grow into owning the social calendar rather than simply executing a calendar created by someone else.

jobs.title: UX Content Strategist
jobs.excerpt: About DripsDrips helps organizations build stronger customer and member relationships through personalized, two-way conversations at scale.
jobs.description:
About Drips

Drips helps organizations build stronger customer and member relationships through personalized, two-way conversations at scale. We combine AI-powered engagement with strategy, design, and managed execution to help people take meaningful next steps across the customer journey.

Our User Experience team turns business goals, user needs, operational realities, and performance insights into clear, useful conversation experiences across channels and use cases.

About the role

We're hiring a UX Content Strategist to join our User Experience team as a full-ownership strategist, driving UX strategy, content direction, conversation design, and client-facing delivery for complex programs from discovery through launch and optimization.

Your primary (but not only) focus will be healthcare, designing member-facing experiences for health plans and healthcare organizations. You'll bring enough healthcare fluency to know the difference between a message that's merely accurate and one that's useful, respectful, motivating, compliant, and appropriate for the moment a member receives it. Payer experience is strongly preferred, but we're open to candidates with other meaningful healthcare experience and a demonstrated ability to learn complex domains quickly.

You'll also flex into other verticals when demand requires it. We're looking for a strategist who can take a problem from ambiguity to a clear, defensible, measurable experience — and explain the reasoning behind the work.

What You'll Do

Own UX strategy end to end

  • Lead discovery and translate client goals, audience needs, operational realities, and program constraints into a coherent UX strategy.
  • Develop conversation designs, scripts, content guides, journey maps, kickoff materials, and optimization recommendations ready for implementation and client review.
  • Make decisions that balance business outcomes, feasibility, brand voice, privacy, legal, and compliance requirements.
  • Own deliverables through review, revision, approval, launch, and post-launch learning, not just the first draft.

Design better experiences

  • Translate complex clinical, payer, benefit, and program information into plain, empathetic, action-oriented language.
  • Recognize when a healthcare message needs additional validation, escalation, or careful handling of privacy and protected health information.
  • Work confidently with client subject-matter experts and internal partners when requirements are incomplete, conflicting, or evolving.
  • Build reusable patterns, frameworks, and guidance that make high-quality healthcare experiences easier to produce consistently.

Partner across the business

  • Serve as a trusted UX partner to Client Success, Solutions Consulting, Implementation, Project Management, Production, Data, and other cross-functional teams.
  • Facilitate or contribute to discovery sessions, kickoffs, conversation design reviews, and optimization discussions.
  • Present your work clearly, explain your rationale, and guide stakeholders toward decisions.
  • Close loops on open questions, surface risks early, and keep work moving without waiting for perfect information.Help improve intake, handoffs, templates, documentation, and operating practices across the UX function.

Use evidence to improve outcomes

  • Connect content and journey decisions to measurable outcomes: engagement, completion, click-through, response, transfer, appointment, conversion, satisfaction, or other program-specific metrics.
  • Interpret performance signals and client feedback to recommend changes to message strategy, cadence, sequencing, calls to action, and journey structure.
  • Frame hypotheses and split tests that are practical to implement and useful for learning.
  • Use emerging tools, including AI-assisted workflows, thoughtfully, with human judgment and rigorous review for quality, brand alignment, privacy, and compliance.

What we're looking for

  • Meaningful professional experience in healthcare, health insurance, health services, digital health, patient or member engagement, or a closely related domain.
  • Strong experience in UX content strategy, content design, or a comparable discipline.
  • Demonstrated ability to own complex work from discovery through delivery: strategy, writing, review, stakeholder alignment, and iteration.
  • Experience turning complex or regulated information into clear, human, action-oriented content.
  • Strong writing and editing judgment across conversational channels such as SMS, IVR, voice, email, web, and surveys.
  • Comfort facilitating meetings and presenting work to clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Ability to work across multiple concurrent programs, prioritize under pressure, and communicate clearly about scope, tradeoffs, timing, and risk.
  • A collaborative approach and a willingness to help improve the system, not just complete individual assignments.

Strongly preferred

  • Experience with health plans, payers, Medicare, Medicaid, quality programs, risk adjustment, HRA or AWV programs, medication adherence, care management, transitions of care, or member engagement.
  • Experience designing for populations with different health literacy, accessibility, language, age, or care needs.
  • Familiarity with healthcare privacy, PHI-sensitive workflows, regulatory review, or client approval processes.
  • Experience with multi-step journeys, branching logic, personalized content, transfer flows, surveys, or conversational AI.
  • Experience using performance data or experimentation to improve content and journey outcomes.
  • Experience creating reusable frameworks, templates, or playbooks that help a team scale.
  • Comfort using AI-assisted tools as a force multiplier while maintaining high standards for human review and accountability.

Cover letter requirements

To be considered for this role, you must submit a brief cover letter that explains your interest in the UX Content Strategist role at Drips. In your letter, highlight your relevant experience in content strategy, content design, healthcare, customer or member engagement, or related fields. Additionally, describe your experience collaborating with cross-functional teams. Please include one example that illustrates your approach to solving a complex content or experience challenge.

jobs.title: Cloud Operations Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Founded in 2010 in The Netherlands, AnywhereNow is a global leader in Enterprise Dialogue Management, with a vision to ensure every employee and customer feels heard, understood, and valued.
jobs.description:
Founded in 2010 in The Netherlands, AnywhereNow is a global leader in Enterprise Dialogue Management, with a vision to ensure every employee and customer feels heard, understood, and valued. With around 240 employees in working from 22 different countries, we partner with over 2,000 leading enterprises, including Mazda, the UN International Organization for Migration, Adecco Group, and the University of Cape Town, to deliver exceptional customer experiences through the power of Microsoft Teams and AI-driven insights. Our commitment to innovation, customer focus, and accountability drives our success.

We are seeking a highly experienced Cloud Operations Engineer to strengthen our South Africa-based team supporting US (Eastern Time) operations.

This role is focused on operating and improving our Azure-based production environments, including infrastructure managed via Terraform and workloads running on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

You will act as a senior technical escalation point (L4), drive automation initiatives, and contribute to reliability-focused improvements across the platform. This role requires strong hands-on Azure expertise, deep troubleshooting capability, and a practical understanding of infrastructure-as-code and Kubernetes operations.

This role is based in South Africa (remote) and requires working hours aligned to US Eastern Time (ET).

Key Responsibilities

  • Operate and maintain Azure production environments, ensuring high availability, performance, and stability.

  • Operational Stability & SRE: Collaborate with the wider CloudOps team to improve platform stability. This includes applying practical SRE principles like reducing manual "toil" through better documentation and helping define proactive alerting thresholds for voice health.

  • Act as an L4 escalation point for complex cloud incidents across compute, networking, storage, identity, and AKS layers.

  • Contribute to and maintain Terraform-managed infrastructure, including reviewing, modifying, and troubleshooting infrastructure-as-code.

  • Operate and troubleshoot AKS clusters and workloads, including cluster health, scaling, networking, ingress, and performance issues.

  • On-Call Rotation: Participate in the Cloud Operations on-call rotation, providing expert-level coverage for critical production incidents.

  • Documentation: Maintain clear, technical operational procedures and "runbooks" for common voice-related troubleshooting scenarios.

Requirements

Why we would like to have a dialogue with you

Ownership & accountability: You don’t just solve problems; you take responsibility for preventing them from recurring.

Communication: The ability to communicate clearly and effectively with individuals across the organization, and to be responsive to their needs and concerns.

Action-oriented: The ability to act quickly and decisively, even in the face of uncertainty, to move projects forward and achieve business goals.

Commitment: The ability to consistently meet or exceed the quality standards expected by customers.

Collaboration: The ability to work effectively with others and to build strong relationships based on trust and mutual respect, recognizing that everyone has something to contribute.

Systems thinking: You understand how small changes impact the broader system, and you consider scalability and long-term impact.

Customer centricity: the ability to provide high-quality service (to customers), including understanding their needs, solving problems, and responding to feedback.

Adaptability: The ability to adjust to changing situations and work effectively in environments that may be uncertain or unpredictable.

﻿﻿Competencies are key, but to be successful in this role you need to bring a few essentials to kickstart the conversation

  • 5+ years of experience in Cloud Operations, Platform Engineering, or SRE-type roles.

  • Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Azure, including VMs, networking, identity, storage, and monitoring.

  • Proven experience working with Terraform in production environments.

  • General Systems Troubleshooting: A methodical approach to isolation—distinguishing between application, network, and provider-level issues in a complex, distributed environment.

  • Strong operational experience with Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

  • Experience building automation using scripting languages such as PowerShell, Python, or Bash.

  • Experience optimizing Azure environments for reliability and cost efficiency.

  • Monitoring Tools: Experience using Azure Monitor to track performance trends.

Some last notes

AnywhereNow is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We accept difference and we thrive on it for the benefit of our employees, our products, and our community.

Please note that we have a background check policy. The background check differs per country and position. If you would like to know more, the recruiters are happy to answer any questions!

Information Security Responsibilities

All employees are responsible for supporting and maintaining the organization’s information security standards. This includes:

  • Adhering to all applicable information security policies, procedures, and guidelines at all times.

  • Protecting company, customer, and partner data from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or loss.

  • Using company systems, devices, and networks in a secure and compliant manner.

  • Promptly reporting any suspected or actual security incidents, breaches, or vulnerabilities to the appropriate team.

  • Completing mandatory information security and data protection training as required.

  • Ensuring that confidential information is handled and stored securely in line with company policies and legal requirements.

Failure to comply with information security responsibilities may result in disciplinary action.

Highlights

Own Azure reliability at scale. Lead L4 incident response, automate with Terraform, operate AKS, and turn SRE principles into resilient, customer‑critical platforms.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.excerpt: The RoleFSM is building the next generation of AI-powered financial systems — where accounting, operations, and data applications work together intelligently.
jobs.description:
The Role

FSM is building the next generation of AI-powered financial systems — where accounting, operations, and data applications work together intelligently. As a Senior Data Engineer, you'll be both a core builder of that platform and a primary technical point of contact for clients as they navigate that transformation.

This is a hands-on, client-facing, senior engineering role. Most of your week is deep technical work — cloud infrastructure, data pipelines, and AI agents. A meaningful part of it is direct conversation with client accounting, finance, and operations teams, leading discovery and translating what you learn into what we ship. You're equally comfortable debugging an IAM policy, pairing with an AI Agent Engineer, and running a discovery session with a client's Controller.

You'll work closely with the Head of Engineering and CTO, alongside FSM's junior and senior engineers and offshore team, and serve as a trusted technical voice clients rely on throughout the engagement.

What You'll Do

1. Cloud & Platform Engineering — the foundation

  • Design, build, and operate FSM's AWS infrastructure: Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, RDS, Cognito, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch.
  • Own infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation), CI/CD (GitHub Actions), and our multi-tenant security model — IAM roles, tenant isolation, secrets management, auditability.
  • Maintain FSM's security and compliance posture — least-privilege IAM, secrets management, and ongoing SOC 2 / Vanta controls, checks, and audit readiness.
  • Maintain and extend our templating/scaffolding system (copier-based) so new client pipelines and agents deploy fast and stay consistent.

2. Data Engineering & Integration

  • Build and maintain data pipelines and the S3-based data platform feeding our agents and BI (DBT, AWS QuickSight).
  • Architect and build integrations across accounting, ERP, CRM, and operational apps — QuickBooks, HubSpot, Stripe, Plaid, Box, Slack — into a clean, source-agnostic layer.
  • Ensure consistent, accurate, reconciled data flow.

3. Agent Development & Implementation

  • Design and code intelligent agents that act on financial data through APIs and natural-language interfaces, plugging into FSM's orchestration layer.
  • Develop the logic frameworks, contracts, and prompts that govern how agents interpret data, take action, and communicate results — including human-in-the-loop controls.
  • Test and refine agent performance with real client data — ensuring security, auditability, and alignment with accounting principles.
  • Client-facing: Walk clients through agent behavior and outputs directly, building their confidence and trust in the automation.

4. Client Discovery & Problem Definition

  • Client-facing: Lead discovery sessions with client accounting, finance, and operations teams to understand their workflows, data challenges, and automation needs.
  • Serve as the primary technical liaison between FSM and the client — explaining findings, options, and trade-offs in terms non-technical stakeholders can act on.
  • Identify opportunities where AI agents can replace repetitive processes, improve reconciliation, or enhance insight delivery.
  • Translate accounting concepts into technical requirements — and technical constraints back into business terms.

5. Documentation, Standardization & Communication (a real, weighted part of the job — not an afterthought)

  • Create comprehensive documentation of automations, agent behaviors, infrastructure, and client-specific implementations.
  • Establish repeatable playbooks, naming conventions, and frameworks that take us from trial-and-error to scalable structure.
  • Partner with leadership to define best practices as the department evolves.
  • Share progress, blockers, and technical decisions clearly — and early — across Engineering, Client Delivery, and CSM, not just with the AI Agent Engineering team.

Requirements

  • 5+ years building and operating production systems on AWS, with real depth in serverless (Lambda/API Gateway), infrastructure-as-code (CloudFormation or similar), and cloud security (IAM, secrets, multi-tenancy).
  • Strong data engineering: Python, SQL, data pipelines, and a modern data stack (DBT, S3/data-lake patterns, a BI tool).
  • Solid CI/CD and Git discipline; you write reviewable code and review others' well.
  • Experience integrating accounting/ERP/CRM platforms (QuickBooks, HubSpot, or similar) via APIs, webhooks, or connectors.
  • Comfort with LLM-based tools and APIs — prompt design and evaluating agent outputs for accuracy and reliability.
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code) as part of your daily development workflow — planning, building, reviewing, and documenting code with them.
  • Demonstrated experience working directly with clients or business stakeholders — leading discovery, presenting findings, managing expectations, not just coding behind the scenes.
  • You take positions and own decisions. Under ambiguity you form a recommendation, explain your reasoning, and drive it — rather than waiting to be told.
  • You communicate clearly under pressure — status, trade-offs, and blockers surfaced early — with technical and non-technical audiences alike.
  • Excellent verbal and written English; strong overlap with US Eastern hours.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience building LLM/AI agents or orchestration systems.
  • Templating tools (copier/cookiecutter).
  • Working knowledge of accounting (reconciliations, journal entries, chart of accounts, financial reporting) — or a genuine willingness to learn the domain; we'll teach it.
  • Experience taking a team from bespoke work toward standardized, documented process.
  • Familiarity with SOC 2 / Vanta-style compliance.

Our Stack

AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, RDS + RDS Proxy, Cognito, Secrets Manager, CloudFormation, CloudWatch) · Python · GitHub Actions · Claude Code · copier · DBT · S3 · AWS QuickSight · LLM agents (Claude) · QuickBooks, HubSpot, Stripe, Plaid, Box, Slack

What Success Looks Like

  • Clients trust you as a technical partner, not just a vendor resource - they bring you problems before they bring you requirements.
  • Discovery sessions consistently surface automation opportunities that convert into shipped agents and integrations.
  • The platform you build is secure, multi-tenant, and reliable - deployments are repeatable and don't bottleneck on any one person.
  • Internal teams (Engineering, Client Delivery, CSM, Leadership) have clear visibility into your work through documentation and proactive communication.
  • Agent deployments are accurate, auditable, and aligned with sound accounting principles — earning continued client confidence.
  • Security and compliance stay audit-ready - SOC 2 / Vanta controls and checks are maintained without last-minute fire drills.

Benefits and Perks

  • Compensation commensurate with experience
  • Unlimited vacation
  • Ongoing education and training
  • Bonuses

  • Draft pleadings, motions, and written discovery
  • Conduct legal research and prepare substantive legal analysis
  • Take and defend depositions
  • Participate in mediations and arbitrations
  • Communicate directly with clients and insurance carriers
  • Collaborate with a team of experienced litigators on complex matters

What We’re Looking For

  • At least 1 year of defense litigation experience
  • Deposition experience required
  • Experience with toxic tort, silica, asbestos, or product liability defense preferred
  • Strong legal research, writing, and advocacy skills
  • Ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities
  • A proactive mindset and ownership of assignments
  • Strong interpersonal and presentation skills

jobs.description:
About the Program:

Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online. Our UX apprentices work through the end-to-end UX design and UX research process for a startup idea of their choice that will help them attract hiring managers in that topic space or industry.

Apprentices take our program for free and receive 1:1 mentorship throughout the 7-month program. Alumni UX apprentices go on to make between $85,000 -$130,000 in UX design, product design, UX research, or service design roles after they complete the program.

We are committed to helping women, immigrants, POC, and LGBTQ folks break into tech and land 6-figure UX jobs. We help you land 6-figure UX jobs or coach you till you get it.

Apprenticeship Requirements:

This apprenticeship program is open to new grads and UX career changers alike! Here are some apprenticeship requirements to keep in mind before applying:

  • Interested in creative career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design
  • Willing to commit 5-10 hours of work per week to complete program deliverables
  • Willing to attend 2-3 hour weekend lectures to learn the end-to-end design process OR willing to complete online video course modules
  • Open to feedback from UX mentors and demonstrates a willingness to revise design work

Apprenticeship Program Learnings:

  • Build digital products and services 0-1
  • Lead end-to-end design process for a startup idea or topic of your choice
  • Lead product scoping and feature scoping, as well as entire project management
  • Identify target market for product and position product for launch success
  • Incorporate AI tools into your UX design process
  • Design AI features and products by considering AI specific design parameters and heuristics
  • Understand how AI works and advocate for ethical AI design that builds trust without over-reliance with users
  • Develop a business model for the product or service and demonstrate how the product/service will scale as the business model scales
  • Lead discovery research by managing user recruitment, creating research plans, writing interview guides, leading 8-16 discovery interviews, and synthesizing interview insights
  • Deliver a compelling UX design and business pitch for your startup idea, showcasing both qualitative and quantitative data to justify the problem space and the solution
  • Tell a compelling story about users by showcasing user types, personas, stakeholder maps, journey maps, process maps, service blueprints, ideation matrixes, sketches, wireframes, UX workflows, prototypes and other visual deliverables
  • Lead user testing of wireframes and prototypes to improve product/service usability and constantly iterate on your startup idea
  • Design a unique design system for your solution from scratch, creating components, a style guide, and branding for your solution
  • Analyze direct and indirect competitors to clearly articulate your solution’s differentiators and why your solution is innovative and more likely to succeed over competing options
  • Consult with startups to create a scope of work and fulfill UX research, UX design, product design and service design work based on your scope of work.

How to Apply:

Please fill out our application form to apply for UX Woman sponsoring your participation in the program. The application takes 5 minutes to complete and will ask you to send in your LinkedIn profile and resume, as well as ask you about why you are interested in this program. You do NOT need to have a UX resume or portfolio to apply- we consider folks who are at the very beginning of their career change, who are still exploring multiple career options.

You will receive UX tips and challenges via email to help you with your transition into UX and will be contacted by us if you are being considered for the apprentice program. Once contacted, you will go through a brief interview process before joining the cohort. Due to the large volume of applicants, we cannot contact all applicants about their application status.If you don’t hear from us about an interview within 2 months of applying, please consider your application closed. We consider applicants on a rolling basis.
