jobs.description:
Are you looking for a Challenge? Looking for an innovative organization and the opportunity to learn and grow professionally? We can help! We are seeking an Adjunct Faculty Instructor NAV104 U.S. National Defense Establishment and Civil-Military Organization – Fall I semester to support the U.S. Navy Community College (USNCC) Adjunct Faculty Support Services. This is a remote opportunity for a 1099 Contractor / Consultant role offering a flexible schedule. Each course requires a 10-week commitment, dedicating eight (8) hours per week. This includes orientation/onboarding, eight (8) weeks of instruction (six (6) hours per week for instruction plus two (2) office hours per week), and one (1) week for final grading and reporting. Instructors can teach up to two (2) courses per term; first-time instructors are limited to one (1) course per term. The Fall I term runs from August 10, 2026 through October 4, 2026.

I’ve never heard of Terrestris. What do you do?

At Terrestris, we leverage technology to create better mission outcomes through better human performance. We form strong client and team relationships through transparency and strive to create an environment where our team can let their excellence shine through. By finding, developing, and incorporating new ideas, we provide memorable services. Rooted in the USMC values of honor, courage, and commitment, Terrestris seeks to deliver extraordinary value to the American people by helping the Government become more efficient and effective.

So, what will the Adjunct Faculty Instructorat Terrestris do?

The Adjunct Faculty Instructor NAV 104 supports the U.S. Naval Community College (USNCC) by delivering high-quality, fully online asynchronous instruction to enlisted Sailors, Marines, and Coast Guardsmen pursuing college-level education. Faculty members teach Naval Studies and/or General Education courses that strengthen critical thinking, leadership, communication, and operational readiness while supporting the Navy's mission of developing a highly educated and mission-ready force.

USNCC courses are delivered through the Blackboard Learning Management System (LMS) in an 8-week online format. Faculty provide engaging instruction, evaluate student performance, facilitate discussions, and deliver timely, meaningful feedback while maintaining the highest standards of academic excellence and professionalism.

What does a typical day look like for an Adjunct Faculty Instructor?

You will:

  • Attend required onboarding and course orientation prior to teaching.
  • Prepare supplemental materials (no more than 10-15%) with current events and/or relevant past experiences for USNCC Dean and/or Associate Dean of the Academics Program approval; upload all materials onto USNCC LMS.
  • Teach assigned undergraduate-level online asynchronous courses in accordance with USNCC policies, syllabi, and instructional standards.
  • Deliver instruction using the USNCC Blackboard Learning Management System (LMS) using the government-provided course shell that includes instructional materials, core lectures, assignments, rubrics, and threaded discussion topics.
  • Facilitate engaging online discussions that encourage critical thinking and active student participation.
  • Grade assignments, examinations, discussion posts, and projects using established grading rubrics.
  • Provide detailed written feedback that promotes student learning and academic success.
  • Monitor student progress throughout the course and proactively identify students who may be at academic risk.
  • Communicate regularly with students and respond to inquiries within established response time requirements.
  • Maintain weekly virtual office hours and additional flexible office hours as needed to support student success.
  • Prepare a weekly progress report.
  • Submit all grades and required documentation within prescribed deadlines.
  • Prepare end-of-course reports summarizing student performance and recommendations for course improvements.
  • Participate in faculty meetings and collaborate with Course Leads, Academic Affairs, and Student Services when required.
  • Maintain current knowledge within the assigned discipline through professional development, scholarship, research, or participation in professional organizations.
  • Ensure all instructional materials and supplemental content comply with USNCC academic policies, copyright requirements, and Department of the Navy standards.

What qualifications do you look for?

You might be the professional we’re looking for if you have:

  • Authorization to permanently work in the United States without sponsorship.
  • Relevant military experience or similar experience in government, and/or working with military personnel.
  • Experience teaching at the collegiate level, in an online learning environment using Learning Management Systems (Blackboard or similar LMS).
  • Appropriate academic credentials and a record of scholarship/research consistent with the assigned teaching role:
    • Demonstrated expertise in U.S. national security studies, American government and politics, comparative politics, public policy, public administration, and American history.
  • Prior experience teaching courses in U.S. politics and government, politics and public policy, U.S. history, U.S. defense policy and/or strategy, civics, and civic engagement.
  • Required Academic OR Professional Qualifications (see below).

Academic Qualifications:

  • A Master's degree (Doctorate preferred) in a relevant discipline.
  • A minimum of 18 graduate semester hours in the teaching discipline.
  • Previous college-level teaching experience.

Professional Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree.
  • Specific, high-level professional experience that is directly relevant to the course’s subject matter in a military or related setting, such as prior military service or experience, particularly in positions of service-wide prominence, and when the experience results in renowned expertise that is aligned with the learning outcomes of the course.
  • Demonstrated teaching experience in an online modality for working adults; must include experience teaching one semester-equivalent course specifically in an online higher education environment at an accredited college or university demonstrating strong student and/or peer evaluation.
  • Demonstrated understanding of Andragogy and Adult Learning Theory.
  • Significant and substantive relevant experience in a military or related setting that makes you uniquely or substantively qualified to teach the specific subject area. This will typically include at least 10-15 years of direct field experience, with at least five of those years at a senior leadership level, in the specific course area being taught.

We are extraimpressed by folks with:

  • Military service or civilian Department of Defense experience, particularly Department of the Navy, US Navy, US Marine Corps, or US Coast Guard.
  • Experience working with military personnel.
  • Extensive subject matter expertise in national security, military operations, leadership, history, government, public policy, or related disciplines.

What kind of benefits does Terrestris Offer?

We offer outstanding benefits including health, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, and work-life programs. Our award programs acknowledge employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our service standards. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in our benefit programs. Other offerings may be provided for employees not within this category.

Terrestris is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status. Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Clean Air Task Force (CATF) is a global nonprofit organization working to safeguard against the worst impacts of climate change by catalyzing the rapid development and deployment of low-carbon energy and other climate-protecting technologies. With 30 years of internationally recognized expertise on climate policy and a fierce commitment to exploring all potential solutions, CATF is a pragmatic, non-ideological advocacy group with the bold ideas needed to address climate change. CATF has offices in Boston, Washington D.C., and Brussels, with staff working virtually around the world.

What You’ll Do

Program Context

CATF works to accelerate the solutions needed to achieve a zero-emissions future. As a leader within the Communications & Marketing team, this role sits at the intersection of audience growth, public engagement, and fundraising, helping connect more people to CATF's mission and impact.

The Director, Mass Market Acquisition and Engagement will lead the strategy for attracting, engaging, and retaining a broad base of mass market supporters while strengthening CATF's fundraising capacity and public influence. Working closely across Communications & Marketing, Development, Events, and program and advocacy teams, this role will build the systems, campaigns, and engagement pathways that help transform interest into action and long-term support.

This is a high-impact leadership role for a marketing professional who can combine strategy, execution, management, analytics, storytelling, and audience insight to expand CATF's reach and accelerate climate progress.

Responsibilities

  • Multi-Channel Marketing Leadership – Build and optimize acquisition programs across digital and emerging channels, including email, paid media, social platforms, search, events, and other audience development opportunities.

  • Fundraising & Revenue Growth – Create scalable donor acquisition and conversion strategies that increase fundraising performance and support key organizational campaigns and giving initiatives.

  • Audience Segmentation & Personalization – Leverage data, analytics, and audience insights to identify target segments and deliver relevant experiences that improve engagement, conversion, and retention outcomes.

  • Engagement Journey Design – Develop effective supporter pathways through content, automation, landing pages, and lifecycle marketing that deepen relationships and inspire meaningful action.

  • Marketing Performance & Optimization – Establish performance metrics and a testing culture that uses experimentation, analytics, and continuous improvement to strengthen results across the marketing funnel.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership – Collaborate closely with Communications & Marketing, Development, Events, Finance, and program teams to align messaging, audience priorities, fundraising efforts, and brand objectives.

  • Team & Vendor Leadership – Foster high-performing internal and external partnerships by providing strategic direction, coaching, and oversight to staff, agencies, consultants, and vendors.

What You'll Bring

You are a strategic and data-driven marketing leader who excels at connecting audiences to meaningful causes. You combine strong judgment with a collaborative leadership style, balancing long-term vision with practical execution. You thrive in complex environments, enjoy solving problems through experimentation and insight, and are energized by helping mission-driven organizations grow their impact.

Required Experience

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 10+ years of progressive experience in digital marketing, audience acquisition, engagement, fundraising growth, or related fields.
  • Demonstrated success developing and executing full-funnel marketing strategies that drive measurable audience, engagement, and revenue outcomes.
  • Experience managing paid media programs and digital marketing channels, including audience acquisition, conversion optimization, retention, and lifecycle engagement.
  • Strong analytical capabilities with experience using performance metrics, segmentation, testing methodologies, and data-driven decision-making to improve results.
  • Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and influencing stakeholders across communications, fundraising, operations, and leadership teams.
  • Proven people leadership experience, including managing, mentoring, and developing staff, agencies, consultants, or vendor partners.
  • Experience working with CRM, marketing automation, and analytics platforms to support engagement and fundraising strategies.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience leading nonprofit fundraising, digital fundraising, or donor acquisition programs.
  • Familiarity with climate, energy, advocacy, public policy, or other mission-driven sectors.
  • Experience with platforms such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Braze, Iterable, Google Analytics, or comparable systems.
  • Exposure to lifecycle marketing, supporter stewardship, and donor retention strategies.
  • Experience supporting geographically distributed or globally operating organizations.
  • Familiarity with emerging marketing technologies, automation tools, artificial intelligence applications, or advanced audience analytics.

What We Provide

Join a team working to accelerate climate solutions while helping build the public engagement and fundraising engine that supports CATF's global impact.

  • A mission-driven role supporting the growth of CATF's audience, influence, and fundraising capacity in the fight against climate change.
  • Exposure to cross-functional collaboration across Communications & Marketing, Development, Events, Finance, executive leadership, and program teams.
  • A collaborative and intellectually curious culture where diverse perspectives are valued and bold, practical solutions to climate change are encouraged.
  • A flexible remote working environment with the ability to work U.S. East Coast hours.
  • A competitive salary range of $145,000-$165,000 USD for U.S.-based employees. Final compensation will be based on experience, qualifications, internal equity, and role alignment. Compensation for employees based outside the United States will be determined according to local market practices and CATF's global compensation framework.
  • An excellent benefits package and a competitive salary based on experience and location.

Ready to Apply?

If you’ve made it this far, you should go ahead and apply. You don’t need to meet every requirement to be a strong candidate. If this role aligns with how you like to work and the kind of impact you want to have, we encourage you to submit your application.

jobs.excerpt: ABOUT VICTORY LIVE Victory Live is a private equity backed technology company aimed at maximizing distribution and yield for live event ticket inventory.
jobs.description:
ABOUT VICTORY LIVE
Victory Live is a private equity backed technology company aimed at maximizing distribution and yield for live event ticket inventory. We provide an end-to-end software platform for the live ticketing industry, managing thousands of sports, theater, and live music event tickets on behalf of artists, promoters, teams, venues, and professional resellers. Victory Live’s comprehensive offerings include an established B2B marketplace, along with both a full-service and an automated SaaS platform to handle all elements of the ticket sales lifecycle, from ingestion to sales fulfillment.

THE POSITION
Victory Live is looking for a Staff Software Engineer to own the technologies and processes that power our B2B marketplace on Ruby on Rails and Hanami. You'll ship features across several business-critical monoliths and microservices, retire technical debt, and set the standards other engineers build against. This is a chance to shape one of our main revenue engines at a premier live event ticketing company.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Collaborate across teams to influence engineering work, ensuring decisions align with divisional strategy.
  • Drive large-scale technical initiatives in our Rails and Hanami services, solving highly complex problems and shipping scalable, secure solutions.
  • Provide guidance and support to engineers, helping them grow and work through hard technical problems.
  • Work with Architects to design and implement system-level solutions within company standards.
  • Define and promote engineering best practices across teams, from RSpec coverage to service boundaries.
  • Identify and pay down technical debt in legacy Rails code to keep it maintainable.
  • Hold the team's code to a high bar through rigorous review, consistent with our quality program.
  • Write high-quality code yourself on the most complex and critical work.

REQUIREMENTS

  • 10+ years of professional software development experience.
  • Strong proficiency in Ruby on Rails; experience with Hanami is a plus.
  • Strong experience building and maintaining high-throughput backend services and APIs at scale.
  • Deep understanding of software engineering best practices.
  • Familiarity with the rest of our stack: Redis, Kafka, Postgres, Datadog, Grafana, Kubernetes, Helm, Kong, Terraform, Docker, GitHub.
  • Familiarity with AWS services such as RDS, ElastiCache, CloudSearch, EKS, and MSK.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Knowledge of live ticket sales or experience working within a fast-paced industry.
  • Mentorship and leadership experience guiding onshore and offshore teams.
  • Genuine interest in growing the engineers around you and shaping team culture, even without a formal management track.

WHY VICTORY LIVE

  • You'll build the infrastructure live events run on; millions of tickets, hundreds of venues, many of the largest teams and events in the world.
  • A lean team where decisions move fast and your code reaches real fans, often the same week.
  • Every release has stakes. Every improvement is felt.
  • High expectations, low tolerance for politics, and a culture built on writing well and shipping with care.

OUR VALUES
We build the systems that power live event ticketing, and we hold a high bar for how we do it. Four principles run through everything:

  • Quality of life. Sustainable processes over heroics. Nobody should be a single point of failure, and nobody should be afraid to take a vacation.
  • Quality of code. Clarity over cleverness. If a teammate needs a long explanation to follow your code, it needs simplifying. Tests prove your work; they aren't optional.
  • Protection of production. Every change is reviewed, tested, and observable. We build with monitoring in mind from day one so we find problems before our users do.
  • Shared knowledge. We work across time zones, so we communicate in the open. Questions go in channels, not DMs, and one answer becomes shared knowledge.

ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
We are an AI-native engineering team. Here is what that looks like in practice:

  • AI-assisted engineering. Every engineer uses Claude, Claude Code, Copilot, and agentic tooling as a routine part of their workflow.
  • Async-first. Most decisions happen in writing through Jira, Confluence, PR descriptions, design docs. We over-communicate on changes and under-communicate on noise.
  • Ownership mindset. Engineers are responsible for what they write and no code reaches production without review. Reviewers are co-owners.
  • Observability is part of "done." If the on-call engineer can't understand a system without reading source, more logging, metrics, and dashboards are needed.
  • Preservation of quality of code and life. We write code that is clean, tested, and maintainable so it serves us well over time, and we build sustainable processes so no one burns out or becomes a single point of failure.
  • Shared knowledge and continued education. We grow as a team by learning from each other through reviews, documentation, and collaboration.

OUR STACK & WAYS OF WORKING

  • Ruby on Rails and Hanami power our B2B marketplace, distribution integrations, and partner-facing APIs
  • Web & mobile clients, REST APIs, microservices
  • Frameworks and tools: Rails, Hanami, Sidekiq, Puma, ActiveRecord, RSpec, RuboCop
  • Data: Postgres, Redis, Kafka
  • Cloud & infra: AWS (RDS, ElastiCache, CloudSearch, EKS, MSK), Kubernetes, Helm, Kong, Terraform, Docker
  • AI tooling: Anthropic / Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, in-house agentic workflows
  • Observability: Datadog, Grafana, Elastic/Kibana, OpsGenie
  • Collaboration: Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Slack, Miro
  • Async-first, agile cadences, distributed onshore + offshore teams

BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Comprehensive medical coverage
  • 100% employer-paid dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Paid time off and company holidays
  • Employee wellness and professional development opportunities

Victory Live is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, Veteran status, or another other characteristic protected by state, local or federal law.

jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Insurance Finance

Corporate Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Risk Management

Regulatory Reporting

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

Strong in complex financial decision-making

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you’ll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs

Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. jobs.excerpt: About the Program:Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online.
jobs.description:
About the Program:

Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online. Our UX apprentices work through the end-to-end UX design and UX research process for a startup idea of their choice that will help them attract hiring managers in that topic space or industry.

Apprentices take our program for free and receive 1:1 mentorship throughout the 7-month program. Alumni UX apprentices go on to make between $85,000 -$130,000 in UX design, product design, UX research, or service design roles after they complete the program.

We are committed to helping women, immigrants, POC, and LGBTQ folks break into tech and land 6-figure UX jobs. We help you land 6-figure UX jobs or coach you till you get it.

Apprenticeship Requirements:

This apprenticeship program is open to new grads and UX career changers alike! Here are some apprenticeship requirements to keep in mind before applying:

  • Interested in creative career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design
  • Willing to commit 5-10 hours of work per week to complete program deliverables
  • Willing to attend 2-3 hour weekend lectures to learn the end-to-end design process OR willing to complete online video course modules
  • Open to feedback from UX mentors and demonstrates a willingness to revise design work

Apprenticeship Program Learnings:

  • Build digital products and services 0-1
  • Lead end-to-end design process for a startup idea or topic of your choice
  • Lead product scoping and feature scoping, as well as entire project management
  • Identify target market for product and position product for launch success
  • Incorporate AI tools into your UX design process
  • Design AI features and products by considering AI specific design parameters and heuristics
  • Understand how AI works and advocate for ethical AI design that builds trust without over-reliance with users
  • Develop a business model for the product or service and demonstrate how the product/service will scale as the business model scales
  • Lead discovery research by managing user recruitment, creating research plans, writing interview guides, leading 8-16 discovery interviews, and synthesizing interview insights
  • Deliver a compelling UX design and business pitch for your startup idea, showcasing both qualitative and quantitative data to justify the problem space and the solution
  • Tell a compelling story about users by showcasing user types, personas, stakeholder maps, journey maps, process maps, service blueprints, ideation matrixes, sketches, wireframes, UX workflows, prototypes and other visual deliverables
  • Lead user testing of wireframes and prototypes to improve product/service usability and constantly iterate on your startup idea
  • Design a unique design system for your solution from scratch, creating components, a style guide, and branding for your solution
  • Analyze direct and indirect competitors to clearly articulate your solution’s differentiators and why your solution is innovative and more likely to succeed over competing options
  • Consult with startups to create a scope of work and fulfill UX research, UX design, product design and service design work based on your scope of work.

How to Apply:

Please fill out our application form to apply for UX Woman sponsoring your participation in the program. The application takes 5 minutes to complete and will ask you to send in your LinkedIn profile and resume, as well as ask you about why you are interested in this program. You do NOT need to have a UX resume or portfolio to apply- we consider folks who are at the very beginning of their career change, who are still exploring multiple career options.

You will receive UX tips and challenges via email to help you with your transition into UX and will be contacted by us if you are being considered for the apprentice program. Once contacted, you will go through a brief interview process before joining the cohort. Due to the large volume of applicants, we cannot contact all applicants about their application status.If you don’t hear from us about an interview within 2 months of applying, please consider your application closed. We consider applicants on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: Digital Marketing Manager - Consumer Acquisition
jobs.excerpt: The MissionDementia affects 7 million Americans — and the family members caring for them carry a burden no system was built to support.
jobs.description:
The Mission

Dementia affects 7 million Americans — and the family members caring for them carry a burden no system was built to support. Ceresti is changing that. We are the nation's leading dementia management provider, purpose-built to activate family caregivers through personalized education, coaching, and tech-enabled monitoring. Independent analyses demonstrate >40% medical cost reductions for the populations we serve.

As we scale our dementia management program nationwide, we need someone who can find the caregivers who need us — and bring them into the program with rigor, empathy, and speed.

The Role

You are the performance engine behind Ceresti's consumer acquisition engine. You own paid media, funnel optimization, and lifecycle marketing end-to-end. You are accountable for caregiver acquisition cost, enrollment velocity, and the channel mix that gets us there.

You will report to the Director of Marketing and partner closely with our Client Success, Product, and Operations teams. You will build the digital acquisition function from the ground up — and grow it as the program and capabilities expand.

This is not a brand marketing role. It is a performance role with a clinical mission behind it. You will need both: the expertise to understand and optimize CAC, and the empathy to understand that every click represents a family in the middle of one of the hardest experiences of their lives.

What You'll Own

Paid Acquisition

  • Plan, execute, and optimize paid campaigns across Meta, Google, programmatic display, and emerging channels (CTV, native, audio).
  • Manage a six-figure annual paid media budget with full P&L accountability — own CAC targets, channel ROI, and quarterly forecasts.
  • Build, test, and iterate creative concepts in partnership with the Director of Marketing — copy, imagery, landing page variants.

Funnel & Conversion

  • Build and continuously optimize landing pages, lead capture flows, and the caregiver enrollment funnel.
  • Own A/B testing roadmap across creative, audience, and funnel stages — codify what works into a repeatable playbook.
  • Partner with engineering and operations to instrument tracking, attribution, and analytics infrastructure (GA4, server-side tagging, consent management).

Lifecycle & Activation

  • Design and operate email and SMS nurture sequences that move caregivers from interest to enrollment to activation.
  • Build cohort-based lifecycle programs that support caregiver retention and program engagement.
  • Partner with the clinical team to ensure messaging reflects the lived reality of family caregiving — never generic, never tone-deaf.

Analytics & Reporting

  • Build the weekly and monthly performance reporting cadence — CAC, LTV, channel mix, cohort behavior, funnel health.
  • Translate data into recommendations leadership can act on. Tell the story behind the numbers.
  • Maintain Medicare compliance and HIPAA-conscious data hygiene across the marketing stack.

Cross-Functional Support

  • Support B2B demand generation as a secondary motion — LinkedIn campaigns, ABM tactics, conference follow-up flows.
  • Hold the line on brand consistency in every consumer-facing execution.

What You Bring

Required

  • 4–7 years of hands-on healthcare digital marketing experience with a clear focus on direct-to-consumer performance marketing.
  • Creativity and cutting-edge digital marketing proven success with precision marketing adjacent experience.
  • Proven track record managing paid media budgets of $500K+ annually with documented CAC, ROAS, or conversion outcomes you can speak to specifically.
  • Deep, current expertise in agentic AI marketing, Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads, and at least one programmatic or emerging channel.
  • Hands-on fluency with GA4, attribution platforms, and modern marketing analytics — not just dashboard consumption.
  • Experience building landing pages and conversion flows.
  • Experience operating email/SMS lifecycle platforms (Klaviyo, Customer.io, HubSpot Marketing Hub, or equivalent).
  • Comfort with ambiguity and shifting priorities — this is a startup, and the priorities will evolve.
  • A demonstrable ability to hold rigor and empathy in the same hand. You take numbers seriously. You also take people seriously.

Strongly Preferred

  • Healthcare DTC experience — particularly Medicare-age consumers, family caregivers, or chronic condition populations.
  • HIPAA-adjacent marketing experience and familiarity with healthcare compliance constraints.
  • Experience marketing to caregivers, adult children of aging parents, or aging-in-place audiences.
  • Familiarity with healthcare value-based care, Medicare Advantage, or CMS program contexts.
  • Background in startup environments where you built something from zero to scale.

Why This Role Is Different

Performance marketing roles in healthcare often live in one of two bad places: pure DTC shops where the work is high-volume and low-meaning, or healthcare orgs where the marketing function is treated as an afterthought to clinical operations.

This role is neither. The work is mission-critical to caregivers navigating dementia. The numbers matter because the outcomes matter. You will see, in cohort data, the families you helped reach. That is rare. We do not take it for granted.

Logistics

  • Location: Remote within the U.S. Occasional travel for team offsites and key conferences.
  • Compensation: Competitive base salary, meaningful equity, and benefits aligned to senior individual contributor talent in healthcare technology.
  • Benefits: Health, dental, vision, PTO, and a culture that respects the boundary between work and the rest of your life.
  • Reporting line: Director of Marketing
  • Start date: As soon as the right person is in place.

How to Apply

Send us your résumé and a short note (no formal cover letter needed) telling us about one campaign you ran that you are genuinely proud of — and what you learned from it. We read every one.

Our interview process includes a 60-minute working session where you will walk us through how you would approach a real Ceresti acquisition challenge. We design it to be useful for you, not just diagnostic for us.

Seeing dementia differently changes everything.

Ceresti Health is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that reflects the diversity of the families we serve.

Vantage Point Solutions (VPS) is seeking a Substation Engineering Lead to provide technical leadership, project

through commissioning.

The Substation Engineering Lead is responsible for the technical direction, design oversight, and professional

engineering approval of substation projects. This role provides mentorship and leadership to engineers, manages

project execution, and ensures projects are completed safely, with quality, on schedule, and within budget.

Successful candidates demonstrate strong leadership, sound engineering judgment, adaptability, attention to

detail, and a commitment to delivering exceptional service.

Why Vantage Point Solutions?

Vantage Point Solutions was founded in 2002 on the belief that people come first. Today, VPS is a customer

focused, technology-driven engineering and consulting firm serving clients in the power, broadband, and

financial industries.

We are committed to delivering exceptional service while fostering a culture built on teamwork, accountability,

respect, innovation, and professional growth. Our employees are empowered to make meaningful contributions

to our clients, communities, and industries while building rewarding careers.

Technical Leadership & Project Management:

  • Lead and manage multiple substation projects simultaneously from planning through construction and commissioning.
  • Conduct quality assurance and quality control reviews throughout all phases of project delivery.
  • Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in compliance with local, state, and federal technical, regulatory, and safety standards.
  • Conduct quality assurance and quality control reviews throughout all phases of project delivery.
  • Develop project scopes, schedules, budgets, and engineering cost estimates.
  • Stay current with applicable codes, standards, industry practices, and emerging technologies.

Engineering & Design:

  • Develop, review, and approve (PE-seal) complete substation designs, including physical layouts, electrical design, grounding systems, equipment selection, bus configurations, structural steel, protection and control systems, relay schematics, wiring diagrams, SCADA integration, and bills of material to deliver full construction drawings (IFC) and bid packages (IFB).

  • Professionally seal for-construction substation designs, protection and controls, and grounding system designs.

Client & Field Support:

Job Overview

We are looking for a reliable, patient-focused, and experienced Dental Medical Receptionist to join our remote healthcare team. The ideal candidate will have 3+ years of hands-on experience working in a U.S. dental practice and a strong understanding of dental front-office operations, patient communication, scheduling, insurance verification, pre-authorizations, and dental terminology.

The successful candidate must be comfortable communicating with patients in English and have practical experience working with dental insurance, treatment plans, dental coding, and pre-authorization processes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage inbound calls, emails, and patient inquiries in both English and Spanish.
  • Schedule, reschedule, and confirm dental appointments.
  • Handle patient check-in and check-out processes.
  • Verify patient demographics, insurance eligibility, and dental benefits.
  • Review insurance benefits, including copays, deductibles, annual maximums, waiting periods, and coverage limitations.
  • Obtain and follow up on dental insurance pre-authorizations and pre-determinations.
  • Assist with treatment plan coordination and communicate insurance-related information to patients.
  • Process patient payments and follow up on outstanding balances.
  • Coordinate appointment reminders, recalls, and patient follow-ups.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date patient records and documentation.
  • Communicate effectively with dentists, hygienists, dental assistants, insurance companies, and other dental staff.
  • Support dental claims and other insurance-related administrative processes as needed.
  • Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with HIPAA requirements.
  • Provide general administrative and front-desk support to ensure smooth daily dental practice operations.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience as a Dental Receptionist, Dental Front Desk Coordinator, Dental Administrative Assistant, or similar role in a U.S. dental practice.
  • Previous experience working remotely in a dental setting is required.
  • Fluent in English, with strong verbal and written communication skills .
  • Strong knowledge of dental office workflows, terminology, scheduling, and patient coordination.
  • Hands-on dental insurance pre-authorization/pre-determination experience — not just theoretical knowledge.
  • Strong experience with dental insurance verification, including eligibility, benefits, coverage requirements, deductibles, copays, and annual maximums.
  • Working knowledge of dental coding and CDT codes.
  • Understanding of dental procedures, treatment plans, and common dental terminology.
  • Basic understanding of dental X-rays and the ability to identify or understand common types of dental radiographs and terminology.
  • Strong patient service and communication skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
  • Proficiency with computers, electronic health/dental records, and dental practice management software.
  • Ability to work independently and maintain productivity in a fully remote environment.
  • HIPAA knowledge or certification is preferred.

Preferred Dental Practice Management Experience

Experience with one or more of the following dental practice management systems is highly preferred:

  • Dentrix / Dentrix Ascend
  • Eaglesoft
  • Open Dental
  • Curve Dental
  • Or other comparable dental practice management systems.

Preferred Additional Experience

  • Dental insurance claims and follow-up.
  • Dental pre-authorizations and pre-determinations.
  • Treatment plan coordination.
  • Dental coding and CDT codes.
  • Understanding of dental X-rays and radiographic terminology.
  • Insurance benefit breakdowns and verification.
  • Patient billing, payment processing, and outstanding balance follow-up.

The ideal candidate is a bilingual dental professional with strong front-office experience who can confidently communicate with patients, verify dental insurance benefits, navigate pre-authorization requirements, understand CDT codes and dental terminology, and provide administrative support with minimal supervision.

This is not a general medical receptionist position. Hands-on dental practice experience and practical knowledge of dental insurance processes are essential.

jobs.description:
About Concept Plus

Concept Plus is a mission-focused technology solutions provider that transforms IT concepts into impactful solutions for federal agencies. Headquartered in Fairfax, VA, we bring the agility, responsiveness, and customer intimacy of a small business combined with the quality and infrastructure of a larger firm.

Recognized as an award-winning Oracle partner, we have delivered innovative solutions across Defense, Intelligence, Civilian, Health IT, and Tribal sectors. Our highly certified experts build systems that drive efficiency, accelerate modernization, and ensure mission outcomes with certainty.

We offer competitive pay, comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance, paid life insurance, paid time off, 11 paid holidays, performance bonuses, tuition reimbursement, unlimited training, and the opportunity to thrive in a collaborative, flexible, and innovative environment.

For more information, visit .

About the role

Concept Plus is seeking an experienced Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Engineer to support the transition of a mission-critical Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) environment from on-premises infrastructure to Oracle Cloud Exadata Infrastructure. This role will focus on architecting, deploying, and optimizing OCI resources required for EBS, ensuring the solution meets stringent government security, availability, and performance requirements. A key responsibility will be designing and implementing cross-region disaster recovery (DR) for EBS within OCI to ensure continuity of operations (COOP) and mission resilience.

What you'll do

  • E-Business Suite Cloud Migration
    • Lead the end-to-end migration of a mission-critical EBS environment from on-premises to OCI, including planning, architecture, deployment, data migration, and cutover support.
    • Assess current on-prem environments and design target OCI architectures that align with performance, availability, security, and government compliance requirements.
    • Architect and configure OCI components required for EBS: Compute, Block Storage, Object Storage, VCN, Load Balancing, File Storage, Database services, and identity/security services.
    • Coordinate with DBA, application, and network teams to ensure successful migration of application tiers, database tiers, and custom EBS integrations.
  • Cross-Region Disaster Recovery for E-Business Suite
    • Design, build, and validate a cross-region DR architecture for EBS using OCI services such as block volume replication, database Data Guard, object storage replication, and load balancer failover strategies.
    • Implement automated replication, failover, and recovery procedures for both the EBS application tier and database tier.
    • Develop COOP/DR runbooks, testing plans, and failover/failback procedures tailored to mission-critical government workloads.
    • Lead periodic DR tests and ATO-aligned validation exercises to ensure readiness for region-wide outages.
  • Cloud Architecture, Security & Compliance
    • Ensure all EBS migration and DR activities adhere to federal standards including FedRAMP, FISMA, and NIST 800-53 security controls.
    • Configure IAM policies, compartments, network security groups, WAF, encryption (KMS), and audit logging to meet government governance requirements.
    • Support security assessments, SSP updates, ATO processes, and POA&M resolution activities for cloud-hosted EBS systems.
  • Operational Support & Optimization
    • Monitor OCI infrastructure supporting EBS workloads for performance, cost, and reliability; implement tuning and scaling strategies as needed.
    • Develop and implement patching strategies for EBS components hosted in OCI, including coordination across environments (DEV/TEST/STAGE/PROD).
    • Troubleshoot EBS-related cloud issues including performance bottlenecks, networking, replication issues, or cross-region failover behavior.

jobs.description:
Job Overview:

We are looking for an experienced Senior Estimator to support the preconstruction and estimating operations of a U.S.-based commercial construction company.

This is a senior-level construction estimating role focused primarily on full-cycle estimating, while also contributing to trade partner development and AI-enabled process improvement. The successful candidate will take ownership of estimating work from bid intake and document review through quantity takeoffs, pricing, subcontractor solicitation, bid leveling, estimate assembly, and internal review.

The ideal candidate is a construction professional with strong estimating judgment, mathematical accuracy, excellent attention to detail, and the confidence to communicate directly with U.S.-based subcontractors and trade partners.

Job Details:

  • Work set up: Work from Home
  • Schedule: Monday to Friday | 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Central Time | 9:00 PM-6:00 AM Manila Time
  • Holiday: Will follow US holiday calendar

Responsibilities:

Estimating & Preconstruction – 70%

  • Manage assigned projects through the full-cycle estimating process, from bid intake through internal review and handoff.
  • Review invitations to bid, drawings, specifications, addenda, bid forms, schedules, alternates, allowances, and submission requirements.
  • Maintain organized bid documentation, including bid calendars, document registers, addenda logs, and estimate status trackers.
  • Read and interpret architectural, structural, civil, MEP, specialty, and vendor documents and translate project requirements into scopes, quantities, and cost components.
  • Identify scope gaps, drawing conflicts, missing information, constructability concerns, long-lead items, and other project risks.
  • Perform detailed and auditable quantity takeoffs using consistent measurement methods, plan references, units, assemblies, waste factors, and revision controls.
  • Develop labor, material, equipment, subcontractor, general conditions, permits, freight, taxes, escalation, allowances, and contingency components as applicable.
  • Prepare trade-specific scopes and solicit competitive bids from qualified subcontractors and suppliers.
  • Analyze and level subcontractor proposals by reviewing inclusions, exclusions, qualifications, alternates, unit rates, schedules, lead times, and commercial risks.
  • Prepare clear assumptions, clarifications, exclusions, RFIs, and risk items for management review.
  • Develop a clear Basis of Estimate documenting the project basis, scope, methodology, pricing, quotes, assumptions, allowances, exclusions, and risks.
  • Reconcile quantities, formulas, units, extensions, markups, and estimate totals and perform thorough quality checks before review.
  • Support conceptual, schematic, budget, negotiated, hard-bid, change-order, and value-engineering estimates as applicable.
  • Prepare estimates for internal review and clearly communicate the cost rationale, assumptions, and outstanding risks.
  • Support the conversion of awarded estimates into useful turnover information for project execution and procurement.
  • Capture bid results and estimate-to-actual feedback to improve future estimating accuracy.

Trade Partner Development – 20%

  • Build and maintain a strong network of qualified subcontractors and suppliers across relevant markets.
  • Identify potential trade partners based on trade specialty, geography, project type, capacity, and project requirements.
  • Conduct professional outbound calls and email outreach to U.S.-based subcontractors and suppliers.
  • Introduce qualified trade partners to bidding opportunities and maintain ongoing professional relationships.
  • Learn each trade partner's capabilities, service areas, capacity, and project preferences.
  • Prepare targeted invitations to bid rather than relying on mass outreach.
  • Maintain accurate relationship records, including contact history, bidding participation, quote quality, and follow-up actions.
  • Support the qualification process by gathering relevant company, licensing, insurance, safety, capacity, and project experience information.
  • Help re-engage inactive or high-potential trade partners.
  • Monitor trade partner participation, responsiveness, reliability, and overall performance.

AI & Process Improvement – 10%

  • Identify opportunities to improve estimating efficiency, accuracy, and consistency through AI, automation, data, and workflow improvements.
  • Explore practical applications of AI for document review, addenda comparison, RFI drafting, proposal analysis, data organization, and repetitive estimating tasks.
  • Identify opportunities to improve subcontractor sourcing, follow-ups, relationship management, and bid coverage through technology.
  • Support the development of repeatable workflows, checklists, SOPs, templates, and reporting tools.
  • Test proposed improvements against known results and maintain appropriate human review and quality controls.
  • Ensure AI-assisted outputs are verified against source documents and do not replace professional estimating judgment.
  • Document successful process improvements so they can be consistently adopted by the broader team.

Qualifications:

Required

  • At least 5 years of experience in construction estimating, quantity surveying, or preconstruction.
  • Experience supporting U.S.-based construction projects or projects with comparable construction standards and estimating practices.
  • Strong full-cycle estimating experience, beyond quantity takeoff, including bid planning, scope development, subcontractor solicitation, quote analysis, bid leveling, estimate documentation, internal review, and handoff.
  • Ability to confidently read and interpret architectural, structural, civil, MEP, and specialty construction documents.
  • Strong mathematical and analytical reasoning skills, including dimensions, conversions, production rates, labor assumptions, waste, freight, taxes, escalation, markups, and reconciliation.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and the ability to work with structured tables, formulas, lookups, pivot tables, validation, and error checks.
  • Strong document control and attention to detail.
  • Strong written and spoken English communication skills.
  • Comfortable making outbound calls to U.S.-based subcontractors and trade partners, asking scope-related questions, following up on bids, and building professional relationships.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple estimates, deadlines, and follow-ups.
  • Ability to work independently while maintaining clear communication and escalating issues early.
  • Reliable internet connection, backup connectivity/power, and a professional remote work environment.

Preferred / Nice-to-Have:

  • 5+ years of construction estimating or preconstruction experience.
  • Experience with commercial construction, particularly commercial buildouts.
  • Experience across multiple construction sectors such as residential remodeling, civil/site work, structural steel or fabrication, or pre-engineered metal buildings.
  • Knowledge of CSI MasterFormat.
  • Experience with conceptual and detailed estimating, design-build preconstruction, value engineering, procurement strategy, or estimate-to-actual analysis.
  • Experience developing or managing a subcontractor sourcing, qualification, CRM, bid participation, or performance management program.
  • Experience with takeoff and construction platforms such as Bluebeam Revu, PlanSwift, STACK, On-Screen Takeoff, Procore, or comparable tools.
  • Experience with construction management, ERP, CRM, or document management platforms.
  • Exposure to AI tools, automation, workflow orchestration, Power Automate, Make, Zapier, n8n, Python, APIs, Power BI, or similar technologies.
  • Demonstrated experience using AI or automation to improve a real business workflow is a strong advantage.
  • Degree or formal training in construction management, civil engineering, architecture, quantity surveying, cost engineering, mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Professional training or certification through organizations such as ASPE, AACE, or RICS is a plus.

jobs.description:
Family Office Investment Services Manager

About the Role

FSM seeks a CFA Charterholder to lead investment services delivery — and directly manage capital — across a growing roster of ultra-high-net-worth client families. This role carries a dual mandate: you are both the institutional framework builder who ensures every advisor is tracked, benchmarked, and held accountable, and a discretionary portfolio manager with direct responsibility for assigned capital sleeves within each client's overall allocation.

This is a rare seat for a CFA who has managed real money, is fluent in multi-asset portfolio construction, and can simultaneously operate at the orchestration level — sitting above a roster of outside managers — and at the execution level, managing positions directly. You will not be a passive scorekeeper. You will be in the game.

What You'll Own

Discretionary Portfolio Management

  • Manage assigned capital sleeves across client portfolios on a fully discretionary basis, spanning liquid equities, fixed income, and select alternatives
  • Construct and maintain model portfolios with explicit factor exposures, benchmark targets, and risk budgets approved by the client principal
  • Execute investment decisions including security selection, position sizing, rebalancing, and tactical allocation shifts within the agreed investment policy statement (IPS)
  • Generate time-weighted and money-weighted return reporting on directly managed sleeves, held to the same S&P 500 benchmark standard applied to all outside managers
  • Produce written investment rationale for every material position change — no undocumented trades
  • Coordinate with client tax advisors on tax-lot management, wash sale rules, and the interaction between active trading and the client's broader tax posture

Investment Oversight & Multi-Manager Coordination

  • Maintain and continuously improve performance measurement frameworks for each client's full advisor roster, benchmarked against the S&P 500 and appropriate secondary indices
  • Produce quarterly manager scorecards covering rolling 1-, 3-, and 5-year returns (gross and net of fees), with plain-English summaries written for principals, not advisors
  • Build and maintain pairwise correlation matrices and factor-decomposed diversification analyses across all active managers, including directly managed sleeves
  • Perform look-through concentration analysis to surface true single-name, sector, geography, and thematic exposures across the entire portfolio — including positions you hold directly

Portfolio Analytics & Risk

  • Decompose each manager's results by asset class, sector, and factor exposure (value, growth, size, momentum); apply the same attribution framework to your own directly managed sleeves
  • Develop and maintain liquidity waterfall models under defined stress scenarios, incorporating LP lockups, directly held positions, real estate assumptions, and credit line availability
  • Monitor concentration risk in real time across all sleeves — both managed externally and managed directly — and escalate when aggregate exposures exceed agreed thresholds
  • Partner with the FSM operations team on cross-entity insurance and risk audits, contributing investment-side risk context

Investment Policy & Client Governance

  • Draft and maintain a written Investment Policy Statement (IPS) for each client, covering return objectives, risk tolerance, liquidity requirements, constraints, and benchmark selection
  • Lead quarterly investment review meetings with family principals; present performance of directly managed sleeves alongside outside manager scorecards in a unified format
  • Participate in asset allocation reviews with the client's strategic advisor; provide quantitative support for allocation shift recommendations
  • Translate institutional-grade analytics into direct, no-jargon deliverables that respect client sophistication without burying them in unnecessary complexity

Advisor Coordination & Governance

  • Serve as FSM's primary point of contact for each client's wealth management roster, operating as an objective oversight layer above individual outside managers
  • Facilitate quarterly advisor review sessions; provide written scorecard summaries to the client principal in advance of each meeting
  • Coordinate on capital call timing, distribution reinvestment, and cash management across all sleeves

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, mathematics, or a related quantitative field
  • CFA Charterholder in good standing
  • Series 65 (or Series 66) license, or willingness to obtain prior to assuming discretionary management responsibilities; RIA registration experience preferred
  • 7+ years of experience in investment management, with demonstrated responsibility for managing discretionary capital — not just analyzing or recommending
  • Deep fluency in portfolio construction, performance attribution, factor analysis, and multi-asset risk management
  • Direct experience with investment policy statements, rebalancing frameworks, and client-level reporting for discretionary accounts
  • Demonstrated experience working in or alongside multi-entity family office structures (trusts, LLCs, LP structures, multi-state tax exposure)
  • Proficiency with portfolio management and analytics tools (Addepar, Black Diamond, Orion, Masttro, or equivalents); ability to operate effectively without them when necessary
  • Exceptional written communication — your investment memos and scorecards will go directly to principals

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience as a named portfolio manager on a discretionary account with documented performance track record
  • Experience managing capital in a family office or multi-family office environment, not just an institutional or retail wealth context
  • Familiarity with crypto asset reporting, covered call overlays on concentrated positions, and the tax coordination those strategies require
  • Working knowledge of LP/PE structures, capital call mechanics, and IRR computation for illiquid sleeves
  • Comfort operating without a large support infrastructure — this role rewards self-sufficiency and judgment under ambiguity

What FSM Is Not Looking For

  • Analysts who have recommended trades but never owned the P&L
  • Advisors whose primary value proposition is tax optimization over investment returns
  • Portfolio managers who manage to a style box rather than to a client's actual objectives
  • Candidates who equate glossy client materials with institutional rigor

Who You'll Work With

You will report to FSM's engagement lead and work alongside the FSM operations team, client tax advisors, outside wealth managers, legal counsel, and the family principals themselves. Clients are performance-first, intellectually rigorous, and allergic to theater. You will be held to the same benchmark standard you apply to every outside manager on the roster — and that's exactly the point.

Compensation

Competitive base salary commensurate with experience, performance-based bonus tied to portfolio outcomes, client retention, and deliverable quality, and equity participation in FSM's family office practice as it scales. AUM-based compensation is not the primary structure — by design — though performance incentives tied to risk-adjusted returns on directly managed sleeves are on the table for the right candidate.

Medical Billing Career Opportunity — Experienced & Entry-Level Candidates Welcome

SYDIERA Healthcare Staffing

Are you interested in building a career in medical billing and healthcare administration?

SYDIERA Healthcare Staffing is connecting motivated individuals with opportunities in the medical billing field. We welcome both experienced medical billing professionals and individuals who are new to medical billing and interested in learning the field.

Who We’re Looking For

We are interested in candidates who are:

  • Experienced medical billers, coders, or healthcare administrative professionals
  • Individuals with healthcare experience who want to transition into medical billing
  • Entry-level candidates interested in learning medical billing
  • Detail-oriented and comfortable working with confidential information
  • Reliable, organized, and willing to learn
  • Interested in developing a long-term career in the healthcare revenue cycle

Experience

Experienced candidates: If you already have medical billing, coding, claims, insurance verification, accounts receivable, or healthcare administrative experience, we encourage you to apply.

Entry-level candidates: If you do not have medical billing experience, you may still apply. Depending on your background and the opportunity you are being considered for, medical billing training may be required before placement or consideration for certain positions.

Training requirements, if applicable, will be clearly explained during the candidate information process.

What You May Learn or Work With

Depending on the position and your experience level, medical billing responsibilities may include:

  • Insurance claims and reimbursement processes
  • Patient and insurance information
  • Medical billing software
  • Claims submission and follow-up
  • Payment posting
  • Accounts receivable
  • Denials and appeals
  • Healthcare revenue cycle processes
  • HIPAA and healthcare compliance concepts

Ready to Get Started?

If you’re serious about developing your career in medical billing, we invite you to apply.

Apply today to learn more about the opportunity and next steps.
